lead.headline: A software fix is not proof of a safe outcome.
lead.summary: NHTSA opened recall query RQ26006 on 6 November after reports of Waymo automated vehicles passing stopped school buses following a 2025 software remedy. Australia announced proposed frontier-AI safety obligations on 10 November, while Gemini 4 Carbon reached wider availability. The core question: what proves a control works for affected people?

outlook.label: Verify post-remedy outcomes
outlook.summary: DΩP analysis: a published fix, a regulator's new investigation, a proposed law and a simulation benchmark answer different questions. Record release configurations, representative tests and safe human intervention. The newest NHTSA filing predates Monday and was newly incorporated today; it is not relabelled as a Thursday event.
outlook.quote: Human agency is prime. The person bearing the risk deserves a working remedy.

report.title: After the patch: proof of real-world safety and human recourse
report.standfirst: Thursday 12 November research synthesis, recovered on 13 November: proposed Australian AI safeguards, frontier capability and an open Waymo recall-remedy inquiry.
report.intro: The edition records policy announcements, primary regulatory filings, developer evaluations and historical remediations as different evidence types. The official metrics methodology was not recovered; no aggregate numerical scores, trends or incident grades are assigned.

sections.heading: A completed software update does not close a safety inquiry
sections.body: NHTSA opened recall query RQ26006 on 6 November to assess the adequacy of Waymo's school-bus remedy. Its filing lists Waymo fifth-generation ADS and a population of 2,895 vehicles under review; most reported incidents in the earlier evaluation occurred after completion of the 17 November 2025 remedy. This is an open regulator inquiry, not a completed causal finding. Next: configuration-specific tests and final regulator outcome.
sections.quote: A released remedy must still be tested against the hazard it was meant to address.

sections.heading: Mandatory frontier controls are proposed, not enacted
sections.body: On 10 November, the Australian Government announced an intended six-part frontier AI safety/security framework including development safeguards, independent evaluation, incident reporting, transparency and adaptive standards, to be enforced by a proposed regulator. Enacted text and commencement remain pending.
sections.statLabel: Proposed frontier-AI obligations, not enacted requirements

sections.heading: Google's Carbon release makes evidence scope essential
sections.body: Google expanded availability of Gemini 4 Carbon on 10 November and previewed agent /swarm coordination. Developer-reported cyber-safety rates come from simulated attack distributions rather than field incident populations. New tool and multi-agent configurations require permission checks, monitoring and independent reproduction.

sections.heading: A historical fix and a new alleged intrusion are different evidence classes
sections.body: Check Point's 5 November disclosed ChatGPT HTML preview route was reportedly fixed 18 September and retested by the discoverer. No new evidence changes that scoped result. Reuters published vendor-based allegations of an AI-aided intrusion in Central Asia on 11 November; state attribution and victim confirmation remained unverified during this review.

sections.heading: The affected person is not always the customer
sections.body: Schoolchildren near automated vehicles are non-consenting bystanders; Australian government users and enterprise users face other authority limits. For each system, DΩP proposes testing the authorised human's ability to see, refuse, stop and challenge, with evidence from representative conditions. Three selected cases lack a comparable baseline, and neither numerical Control Debt nor a global agency direction is asserted.

investigativeSummary: NHTSA opened recall query RQ26006 on 6 November after reports of Waymo automated vehicles passing stopped school buses. The inquiry covers 2,895 fifth-generation ADS vehicles, not 2,895 incidents or harmed people. The regulator says a majority of reported events occurred after the software remedy was completed on 17 November 2025. It has not yet made a final finding on cause or adequacy. Schoolchildren, bus drivers and road users are affected bystanders. The public filing lacks a comparable encounter denominator, complete post-remedy count and independent field intervention testing. Waymo told TechCrunch it had improved bus behaviour and received no citations since March 2026. Next verification: current software configuration, realistic stopped-bus tests, outcome evidence and the regulator's conclusion.
